kimagghatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it occurs as kimagghati, which is kiṃ + agghati; the entry is for agghati. The -i is the 3rd singular present ending.
kimagghatī.example_1: 5. [kimagghatī taṇḍulanāḷikā ca, bārāṇasī antarabāhirāni; assapañcasate tāni, ekā taṇḍulanāḷikāti;(syā.)] Kimagghati taṇḍulanāḷikāya, assāna mūlāya vadehi rāja [nāḷikā ca (sī.), nāḷikāya (ka. sī. aṭṭha.)];
kimagghatī.translation_1: “Dost ask how much a peck of rice is worth? Speak, King, of the price of the horses.”
kimagghatī.example_2: Bārāṇasiṃ santarabāhirato [bāhirantaṃ (sī.)], ayamagghati taṇḍulanāḷikāti [kimagghatī vaṇḍulanāḷikā ca, bārāṇasī antarabāhirāni; assapañcasate tāni, ekā taṇḍulanāḷikāti;(syā.)].
kimagghatī.translation_2: “It is worth the whole of Benares, both within and without, this single peck of rice.”

vaṇḍulanāḷikā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of taṇḍulanāḷikā (peck-measure of rice) in a Jātaka verse; nominative singular in the text.
vaṇḍulanāḷikā.example_1: Bārāṇasiṃ santarabāhirato [bāhirantaṃ (sī.)], ayamagghati taṇḍulanāḷikāti [kimagghatī vaṇḍulanāḷikā ca, bārāṇasī antarabāhirāni; assapañcasate tāni, ekā taṇḍulanāḷikāti;(syā.)].
vaṇḍulanāḷikā.translation_1: “It is worth the whole of Benares, both within and without, this single peck of rice.”

phalāsāva.meaning_2: desire for fruit; hope of reward; longing for results
phalāsāva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text phalāsāva = phalāsā + eva, metrically shortened. Subject of samijjhati.
phalāsāva.translation_1: one who hopes for the fruit succeeds.
phalāsāva.translation_2: 8. For those who do not hurry, their heart’s desire is fulfilled;

paṭisandhāra.meaning_2: mutual greeting; friendly reception; courteous exchange
paṭisandhāra.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the verse, with the commentary gloss paṭisanthāra; the metre requires the extra syllable. Nominative singular in the text.
paṭisandhāra.translation_1: Prosperity leads to the virtuous ones who practice mutual greeting.

kaṇḍinaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the phrase kaṇḍinaṃ sallaṃ, 'the arrow's dart'; kaṇḍinaṃ is genitive plural or accusative singular of the adjective kaṇḍi, agreeing with sallaṃ. Alternatively could be read as a derivative of kaṇḍa.
kaṇḍinaṃ.translation_2: Shame on the dart of love that pierces a man deeply;

muccena.meaning_2: name of a month; (in list) Muccena
muccena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it appears as part of a list of names, in the instrumental singular muccena, apparently a month name (like Naḷa); the analysis as a noun from √muc is doubtful.
muccena.example_2: Atibhoti vara [rasa (sabbattha)] māluta pāṇa, muccena naḷaavhayanena bhavanti dasāti.
muccena.translation_2: Atibhoti, Vara, Māluta, Pāṇa, Muccena, Naḷa, are the ten that became like this.

udaddhari.meaning_2: lifted up; raised; took out; pulled out
udaddhari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of uddharati; the word is in the verse, meaning a heavy load was lifted or pulled out. The PEU split U+dhara+ī is doubtful.
udaddhari.translation_2: For him who spoke him fair, he moved a heavy load;

vaṇṇūpaṭibhā.meaning_2: having the appearance of colour; resembling the colour (of); like in colour
vaṇṇūpaṭibhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of vaṇṇūpanibhā (also vaṇṇasannibhā). Compound adjective qualifying gīvā (neck). In the text the form is used attributively in the nominative singular.
vaṇṇūpaṭibhā.example_1: 32. Rudaṃ manuññaṃ rucirā ca piṭṭhi, veḷuriyavaṇṇūpanibhā [vaṇṇūpaṭibhā (syā.), vaṇṇasannibhā (ka.)] ca gīvā;
vaṇṇūpaṭibhā.translation_1: “A pleasing note, a lovely back, and a neck in hue like lapis lazuli;

mapacāyanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text mapacāyanti = maṃ + apacāyanti (sandhi, 'honour me'); the entry is for the verb. The subject ye ... narā is plural, hence the plural ending -anti, though the headword is 3rd singular.
mapacāyanti.example_1: 37. Ye vuḍḍha [vaddha (sī. pī.)] mapacāyanti, narā dhammassa kovidā;
mapacāyanti.translation_1: 37. Those people who honour the aged, proficient in the Dhamma;

nikatyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text (nikatyā). The PEU also gives nikata as an adjective meaning cunning; deceitful.

pādamolumba.meaning_2: seized by the leg; held by the foot
pādamolumba.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading pādamolamba in some editions; describes a goat seized by the leg. Nominative singular in the text.
pādamolumba.example_1: Ajiyā pādamolamba [pādamolumba (sī. syā. pī.)], mittako viya socatīti.
pādamolumba.translation_1: He grieves like Mittaka, who seized the goat by the leg.

mittaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative in the text, addressed to a character. Probably a shortened name of Mittavindaka.
mittaka.example_2: Atha mittaka mātu kapotavaro, tathā veḷūka eḷamūgo rohiṇī;
mittaka.translation_2: Atha, Mittaka, the Mother, the excellent pigeon, so that, Veḷūka, the dull-witted, Rohiṇī;

veḷūka.meaning_2: name of a person (in a Jātaka verse)
veḷūka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the verse; nominative singular in the text. Could also be read as an adjective describing the person (dull-witted per the translation), but the Pāḷi gives no clear basis.
veḷūka.example_1: Atha mittaka mātu kapotavaro, tathā veḷūka eḷamūgo rohiṇī;
veḷūka.translation_1: Atha, Mittaka, the Mother, the excellent pigeon, so that, Veḷūka, the dull-witted, Rohiṇī;

aḷārakkhī.meaning_2: having wide beautiful eyes; with lovely eyes
aḷārakkhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound used as a feminine epithet for a woman in the verse. The text form is nominative singular; the reading aḷārakkhī and the gloss aḷārakkhi suggest a feminine ī-stem adjective, though the compound member akkhi is neuter.
aḷārakkhī.translation_1: But when I won the moon-eyed lady,
aḷārakkhī.example_2: Yato laddhā aḷārakkhī, icchā icchaṃ vijāyathāti.
aḷārakkhī.translation_2: But since I have obtained the wide-eyed one, craving has given birth to craving.

tvevekacciyo.meaning_2: but rather a certain person; than a certain person
tvevekacciyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tu (ind, emphatic 'but, rather') + eva + ekacciyo (adj, 'a certain'). In the verse na tvevekacciyo naro means 'not just any certain person' (i.e. better than an ordinary person). The form is tveva + ekacciyo, not tu + eva + ekacciyo with independent words. Nominative singular agreeing with naro.

araññajā.meaning_2: born in the forest; forest-born; growing in the wilderness
araññajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes trees (rukkhā) in the verses. Nominative plural agreeing with rukkhā.
araññajā.translation_1: the trees born in the forest.
araññajā.example_2: 74. Sādhū sambahulā ñātī, api rukkhā araññajā;
araññajā.translation_2: 74. “United, forest-like, should kinsfolk stand; even trees born in the forest are good [when together];

sigāsī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (Sinhalese, Siamese, PTS editions) for sigālī in the verse; nominative singular in the list of animals and objects.
sigāsī.example_1: 77. Usabhā rukkhā gāviyo gavā ca, asso kaṃso siṅgālī [sigāsī (sī. syā. pī.)] ca kumbho;
sigāsī.translation_1: Bulls, trees, cows, and calves, a horse, a gong, a jackal, and a pitcher;

lābūni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the plural lābūni, which belongs to the same paradigm as lābuka. The spelling lābūni is a variant of lābūkāni. The form is nominative plural.
lābūni.example_2: Pokkharaṇī ca apākacandanaṃ, lābūni sīdanti silā plavanti.
lābūni.translation_2: A pond, raw rice, and sandal-wood, gourds that sink, and quartz that floats.

maṇḍūkiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural maṇḍūkiyo in the verse; the sequel shows it used for frogs generally. The PEU treats maṇḍūkī as the feminine of maṇḍūka.
maṇḍūkiyo.example_2: Maṇḍūkiyo kaṇhasappe gilanti, kākaṃ supaṇṇā parivārayanti;
maṇḍūkiyo.translation_2: Frogs swallow black snakes, and a crow is surrounded by royal golden mallards;

cakkhulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. pī.) of visamacakkhukā in the verse; probably a compound of cakkhu + a suffix -la. Nominative plural.
cakkhulā.example_1: 78. Ubho khañjā ubho kuṇī, ubho visamacakkhukā [cakkhulā (sī. pī.)];
cakkhulā.translation_1: Both are crippled (khañjā), both are crippled (kuṇī), both have squinting eyes;

ḍindimaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (object of vādayanta). Variant readings deṇḍima and ḍiṇḍima; probably a loanword.
ḍindimaṃ.example_1: Athāgamā puttahatāya putto, kharassaraṃ ḍiṇḍimaṃ [deṇḍimaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), ḍindimaṃ (ka.)] vādayantoti.
ḍindimaṃ.translation_1: Then the son of a woman whose son is dead came along, beating a harsh-sounding drum.

svāsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of so (nominative singular of ta-) + asi (2nd singular present of √as 1, atthi). Some editions write sosi. Second person singular in the text.
svāsi.example_2: Svāsi pāsāṇamāsīno, yasmā jīvaṃ na mokkhasīti.
svāsi.translation_2: You are now invested with the stone [wheel], and because of this you shall not be released while still alive.

maṅgali.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it is a name in a list of ten (Ahisīlava, Maṅgali, Pāpikassā, Sataṃnikkha, Katatthavara); the form maṅgali may stand for maṅgalī, a bahubbīhi adjective meaning 'auspicious', or a proper name. Related to maṅgala.
maṅgali.example_2: Ahisīlava maṅgali pāpikassā, sataṃnikkha katatthavarena dasāti.
maṅgali.translation_2: Ahisīlava, Maṅgali, Pāpikassa, Sataṃnikkha, and Katatthavara are the ten.

sosīto.meaning_2: scorched; dried up; withered by heat
sosīto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of sosindo in the verse; a compound adjective describing one afflicted by heat. The form is nominative singular in the text.
sosīto.example_1: 94. Sotatto sosindo [sosīto (sī. syā. pī.), sosino (ka.)] ceva, eko bhiṃsanake vane;
sosīto.translation_1: Chilled by night and scorched by day, and alone in awe-inspiring groves;

upakuṭito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text as upakuṭito (nominative singular). The variant upakūḷito suggests the reading upakūḷita; the sense is 'scorched, burned up' inside (manamhi).
upakuṭito.example_1: Atipaṇḍitena puttena, manamhi upakūḷitoti [upakūlitoti (sī.), upakuṭṭhitoti (syā.), upakuṭito (ka.)].
upakuṭito.translation_1: “By a son who is wisest, I am scorched in my heart.”

bhāyasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Second person singular of bhāyati; the ending -si is written -sī before the following nāga (metrical lengthening). The PEU guide takes it as a form of √bhi; √bhī (fear) fits.
bhāyasī.example_2: Tassa ce bhāyasī nāga, kiso nūna bhavissasīti.
bhāyasī.translation_2: If you fear that, bull elephant, you will surely become emaciated.”

udañcanī.meaning_2: water-drawer; bucket for drawing water from a well; small water pot
udañcanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse the water-drawer is compared to a woman who torments. Nominative singular.
udañcanī.example_2: 106. Sukhaṃ vata maṃ jīvantaṃ [sukhakaṃ vata jīvaṃ (ka.)], pacamānā udañcanī;
udañcanī.translation_2: “A happy life was mine, but that water-drawer [a woman who drags and pesters one like a water-pot] keeps me cooking [in distress];

yathanno.meaning_2: according to food; as (his) food is; eating as
yathanno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of yathā + anna (food). In the verse it occurs as yathanno (nominative singular masculine) modifying puriso. The related tathanna (tathannā) in the same line is its counterpart.
yathanno.example_2: 109. Yathanno puriso hoti, tathannā tassa devatā;
yathanno.translation_2: As a man eats, so eats his devas;

sippaka.meaning_2: name of a pastry or sweetmeat; name of one of the ten foods in the riddle verse
sippaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in a list of foods in the Jātaka verse, probably a kind of cake or confection paired with sukhaka, kuṇḍapūva, etc. Vocative in the text.
sippaka.example_2: Sukhakañca vata sippaka bāhiyā, kuṇḍapūva mahallikakā ca dasāti.
sippaka.translation_2: Sukhaka, indeed, Sippaka, Bāhiyā, Kuṇḍapūva, and the old woman are the ten.

kalaṇḍukāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name used as a vocative in the text; -ti is the quotation particle (kalaṇḍukā ti).
kalaṇḍukāti.example_2: Anuvicca kho taṃ gaṇheyyuṃ, piva [pipa (sī. pī.)] khīraṃ kalaṇḍukāti.
kalaṇḍukāti.translation_2: Having closely examined this, your masters will catch you; so drink the milk, Kalanduka.

mamba.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the list dadhi mamba kaṭāhaka pañcamaka, likely a food-item; perhaps a variant of amba (mango).
mamba.example_2: Kusanāḷisirivhayano ca yasaṃ, dadhi mamba kaṭāhakapañcamako;
mamba.translation_2: Kusanāḷi and the one called Sirī, status, curd, mango, and the one with the pot as the fifth;

abhinādayi.meaning_2: makes resound; causes to echo; fills with sound
abhinādayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text (abhinādayi). Causative of abhinadati; the object daddaraṃ is the hollow/echoing rock.
abhinādayi.translation_2: 4. The lion gave a roar, and made the hollow sound of the mountain resound again;

maññivo.meaning_2: do not despise him; you (pl.) should not think lightly of him
maññivo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading maññivho; probably maññatha (2nd plural, 'you think') with mā, or maññi + vo. CPD takes it as 'do not despise him'. Occurs once, in a Jātaka verse.
maññivo.example_1: Dāṭhini mātimaññittho [maññivo (syā.), maññavho (ka.)], siṅgālo mama pāṇadoti.
maññivo.translation_1: Do not despise him, O fanged one, for this jackal gave me my life.”

adaddahi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text. Variant readings adayhi, adaḍḍhahi, adaṭṭhahi; here adaddahi.
adaddahi.example_1: Santappito sappinā pāyasena [pāyāsena (ka.)], kicchākataṃ paṇṇakuṭiṃ adayhi [adaḍḍhahi (sī. syā.), adaṭṭhahi (pī.), adaddahi (?)].
adaddahi.translation_1: Though fed with ghee and rice, it burned the leaf-hut made with such difficulty.”

upasāḷaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A personal name (proper noun) in the verse, nominative singular. Probably not related to upasāḷha; the commentary may explain it as a name given by chance (yadicchakanāma).
upasāḷaka.example_2: Upasāḷaka bhikkhu salāpavaro, atha mettavaro dasapuṇṇamatīti.
upasāḷaka.translation_2: Upasāḷaka, the bhikkhu, Salāpavara, then Mettavara, and the tenth is the one about the merit.

abhinādeti.meaning_2: makes resound; causes to echo; fills with sound
abhinādeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of abhinadati; 3rd singular present. In the text it governs daddaraṃ, 'makes Daddara resound'.
abhinādeti.example_2: 43. Ko nu saddena mahatā, abhinādeti daddaraṃ;
abhinādeti.translation_2: “Who is it with a mighty cry makes Daddara resound?

uhajjaṃ.meaning_2: having lifted up; having raised; having thrown up
uhajjaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for ohacchaṃ. Looks like an absolutive from ud + √hā (or √hac?) used adverbially; meaning uncertain. Alternative readings: ūhacca, ohaccaṃ.
uhajjaṃ.example_1: Idāni kho taṃ ohacchaṃ [ūhacca (sī. pī.), ohaccaṃ (syā.), uhajjaṃ (ka.)], esā asmāka dhammatāti.
uhajjaṃ.translation_1: Now I shall drop something on you; this is our nature.”

uhadaṃ.meaning_2: defecated on; polluted with excrement; soiled
uhadaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of ūhannaṃ / ūhantaṃ in the verse; the commentarial gloss uhadaṃ means defiled with excrement (past participle). Accusative singular agreeing with agnihuttaṃ.
uhadaṃ.example_1: Aggihuttañca uhannaṃ [ūhantaṃ (sī.), ūhanaṃ (syā.), ūhanti (pī.), uhadaṃ (ka.)], dve ca bhinnā kamaṇḍalūti.
uhadaṃ.translation_1: He has defiled the sacred fire, and two water-jars are broken.

janittaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] According to the PEU analysis jana + ṇitta, but a derivation from √jan with the suffix -itta also fits the meaning 'birthplace'. In the Jātaka verse it pairs with bhavitta ('place of growth') and is nominative singular.

abbhuha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for ubbaha (syā.) in the sense 'pull out (the door-posts)'. An absolutive-like indeclinable form. Some editions prefer ubbaha.
abbhuha.example_1: 64. Omadda khippaṃ palighaṃ, esikāni ca abbaha [ubbaha (syā.), abbhuha (ka.)];
abbhuha.translation_1: “Crush quickly the crossbar, pull out the door-posts;

amboyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of amba + ayaṃ; nominative singular in the verse.
amboyaṃ.translation_2: 71. Once this mango was endowed with colour, scent, and taste;

jambūka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of one of the ten kings (or brothers) in the Jātaka verse; vocative singular in the text, used as a proper name.
jambūka.example_2: Dadhivāhana jambūka sīhanakho, haritayava nāgavarena dasāti.
jambūka.translation_2: Dadhivāhana, Jambūka, Sīhanakha, Haritayava, and Nāgavara are the ten.

marūdvāsu.meaning_2: in the deserts; in the sandy regions
marūdvāsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of maruvāsu (maru + vāsu?), probably maru + udakāsu with sandhi, giving locative plural marūdvāsu (a variant reading of maruvāsu in the same line). Uncertain; word and meaning are inferred from context. maru means desert or sandy place; the locative plural is used in the sentence.
marūdvāsu.example_1: 82. Vijjamānesu vākesu [vijjamānāsu maruvāsu (sī.), vijjamānāsu marūdvāsu (pī.)], vijjamānesu kārisu;
marūdvāsu.translation_1: 82. “While there is bark and while there are workmen,

alaññeva.meaning_2: indeed not enough with the old one; the old one is of no use indeed
alaññeva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text alaññeva purāṇiyā means 'the old one is of no use (to me)'. Sandhi of alaṃ (enough, of no use) + aññāya or aññā (with the old one) + eva (indeed); the middle member's exact form is uncertain.
alaññeva.translation_2: I will make a new bowstring; I have no need of the old one.”

umhayate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present in the text; the prefix u- is rare and the form is irregular. The object is in the accusative (naṃ).

mummurasaddo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs only in the compound mummurasaddo (nominative singular); the word is rare and its etymology is uncertain. The commentary glosses it as 'hot ashes and embers' (thusaggimhi kukkuḷe). Some editions read mummure.
mummurasaddo.example_1: Sayetha poṭṭhapādova, mummure [mummure (syā.), maṃ pure (ka.) mummurasaddo thusaggimhi kukkuḷe ca vattatīti sakkatābhidhānesu] upakūthitoti [upakūsitoti (sī. syā. pī.), upakūlito (ka.)].
mummurasaddo.translation_1: One should lie like Potthapada, burnt up in the hot ashes.”

saṃkaraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) of saṅgaraṃ in the verse; accusative singular. The same line gives saṅgaraṃ, so the word means an agreement or contract made for two months.
saṃkaraṃ.example_1: Dve māse saṅgaraṃ katvā [kāraṃ katvāna (sī. pī.), saṃkaraṃ katvā (ka.)], maṃsaṃ jaraggavaṃ kisaṃ;
saṃkaraṃ.translation_1: Having made an agreement for two months, you gave us meat from a thin, old ox;

sarīradabyaṃ.meaning_2: having a beautiful body; of beautiful appearance
sarīradabyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound adjective; the reading vuḍḍhabyaṃ follows in the verse. Neuter nominative singular in the text.
sarīradabyaṃ.translation_2: “One is good, and one is noble; one has beauty, one has years;

vaddhabyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sinhalese and Pī. editions read vuḍḍhabyaṃ; the text has vaddhabyaṃ. A noun of state meaning 'being old', parallel to dabyaṃ ('being able') and sojaccaṃ in the same verse.
vaddhabyaṃ.translation_1: “One is good, and one is noble; one has beauty, one has years;

sojaccaṃ.meaning_2: good birth; noble descent; nobility of birth
sojaccaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sanskritised sojātya from sujāti + ṇya; the Pāḷi shows the assimilation ty > cc. Nominative singular here, listed with other virtues in the verse. Sujacca is a variant reading.
sojaccaṃ.translation_2: “One is good, and one is noble; one has beauty, one has years;

sādhusīliyaṃ.meaning_2: state of having good conduct; being of virtuous character; good moral habit
sādhusīliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun in -iya from sādhusīla (good conduct). Nominative singular in the text, listed among qualities like sojaccaṃ and sarīradabbaṃ.
sādhusīliyaṃ.translation_2: “One is good, and one is noble; one has beauty, one has years;

kannu.meaning_2: which of them?; which one of them?
kannu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Kaṃ nu → kannu by sandhi. Interrogative ka (which?) + emphatic nu. Also analysed as kaṃ nu or kinnu; context asks 'which of the four'.
kannu.example_1: Brāhmaṇaṃ teva pucchāma, kannu tesaṃ vanimhase [vaṇimhase (sī. pī.)].
kannu.translation_1: Answer me this question, brahmin; of the four, which best appears?”

apiruhaka.meaning_2: name (of a Jātaka verse, beginning 'Apiruhaka'); the Apiruhaka verse
apiruhaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears only in the first pāda of a Jātaka verse listing names (Apiruhaka, Rūpavatī, Musala, Pavasanti, Pokkharaṇī); treated as a fixed name, so stem and pattern are left out. Split and meaning are uncertain: api + ruhaka ('even a growing one'?) is possible, but the word functions as a proper name in the verse.
apiruhaka.translation_2: Apiruhaka, Rūpavatī, Musala, Pavasanti, and the fifth, Pokkharaṇī;

muttimavāṇija.meaning_2: Muttima the merchant; the merchant Muttima
muttimavāṇija.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a merchant in the Jātaka verse. Nominative singular in the text; the compound may also be analysed as mutti + ma + vāṇija.
muttimavāṇija.example_2: Atha muttimavāṇija umhayate, ciraāgata koṭṭha sarīra dasāti.
muttimavāṇija.translation_2: Atha, Muttima, Vāṇija, Umhayate, Ciraāgata, Koṭṭha, and Sarīra are the ten.

sirisapāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of sarīsapa in the text; nominative plural sirisapāni. Sometimes analysed as siri + sapati (serpent).
sirisapāni.example_1: Appamāṇo saṅgho, pamāṇavantāni sarīsapāni [sirisapāni (sī. syā. pī.)];
sirisapāni.translation_1: Infinite is the Order, finite are the creeping things;

metehi.meaning_2: enough of these (mangoes); away with these
metehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Metehi is me + tehi, a sandhi of ime (nominative plural of ayaṃ) with tehi (instrumental plural of ta). The whole phrase alaṃ metehi ambehi means 'enough of these mangoes'. Could also be analysed as me (instrumental of ahaṃ) + tehi, but the sense 'enough of these mangoes' fits better with ime + tehi.
metehi.example_2: 115. Alaṃ metehi ambehi, jambūhi panasehi ca;
metehi.translation_2: 115. Enough of these mangoes, rose-apples, and jack-fruits;

visāṭikaṃ.meaning_2: split open; cracked; burst apart; cleft
visāṭikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the sentence it describes uttamaṅgaṃ (the head) after vibhijjitaṃ; variant readings visāṭikaṃ / vighāṭitaṃ show uncertainty about the exact form. Nominative/accusative singular neuter in the text.
visāṭikaṃ.example_1: Yattha ekappahārena, uttamaṅgaṃ vibhijjitaṃ [visāṭikaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), vighāṭitaṃ (sī. niyya)].
visāṭikaṃ.translation_1: Where at one blow my head was split?”

kandalaka.meaning_2: name of a tree (Datura stramonium; thorn-apple); name of a Jātaka (the Kandagalaka Birth Story)
kandalaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in the title Kandagalaka [kandalaka] jātakaṃ, the tenth Jātaka of the Book of Jātaka verse. The gloss and the PEU entry give kandala as a flowering tree (Datura stramonium); the -ka form is the name used in the title. Sense 'name of a Jātaka' is by extension from the tree.
kandalaka.translation_1: The Kandagalaka Birth Story is the tenth.

tyābhato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text is uncertain: the variant tyābhato and the comment paheḷigāthābhāvo manasi kātabbo suggest a corrupt or riddle verse. Possibly a sandhi of tya + ābhato, 'that one brought here'. The reading is doubtful.
tyābhato.example_1: Dūraṃ gataṃ yena ca avhayanti, so tyāgato [tyābhato (syā. ka.) paheḷigāthābhāvo manasi kātabbo] handa ca bhuñja brāhmaṇa.
tyābhato.translation_1: That which they call for when one has gone far—he has come to you, now eat, brahmin.”

paheḷigāthābhāvo.meaning_2: state of a riddle verse; the case of riddle verses
paheḷigāthābhāvo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text (also tyābhato); not the main reading. Seems a commentarial note intruding into the verse.
paheḷigāthābhāvo.example_1: Dūraṃ gataṃ yena ca avhayanti, so tyāgato [tyābhato (syā. ka.) paheḷigāthābhāvo manasi kātabbo] handa ca bhuñja brāhmaṇa.
paheḷigāthābhāvo.translation_1: That which they call for when one has gone far—he has come to you, now eat, brahmin.”

cūpatapeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably cu + upa + tapeti, a metrical/irregular form; the prefix cu- is unusual and may be a sandhi or scribal variant. In the text cittaṃ cūpatapeti maṃ means 'the mind torments me'; 3rd singular present, causative sense.
cūpatapeti.example_2: 132. So maṃ dahati rāgaggi, cittaṃ cūpatapeti maṃ;
cūpatapeti.translation_2: That fire of passion burns me, and my mind torments me;

seggu.meaning_2: name of a person (a brahmin); Seggu
seggu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative in the text, used to address a brahmin. Unclear derivation; possibly a proper name only.
seggu.example_2: 133. Sabbo loko attamano ahosi, akovidā gāmadhammassa seggu;
seggu.translation_2: “All the world’s on pleasure bent, / Seggu, you know not the ways of the village;

paṭikūṭassa.meaning_2: counter-cheat; one who cheats in return; counter-deceiver
paṭikūṭassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text (paṭikūṭassa kūṭaṃ = the cheating of the counter-cheat). paṭi here means 'in return, back'; kūṭa means 'cheat, trickster'. Sometimes written paṭikūṭa as a separate compound, sometimes analyzed as paṭi + kūṭa.
paṭikūṭassa.example_2: 135. Saṭhassa sāṭheyyamidaṃ sucintitaṃ, paccoḍḍitaṃ paṭikūṭassa kūṭaṃ;
paṭikūṭassa.translation_2: Well-thought is this fraud of the one given to fraud; the cheat has been tricked by a counter-cheat.

nākāle.meaning_2: not at the right time; at the wrong time
nākāle.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + kāle, locative of kāla. In the verse it contrasts with kāle.
nākāle.example_2: 151. Kāle nikkhamanā sādhu, nākāle sādhu nikkhamo;
nākāle.translation_2: It is good to go forth at the right time; it is not good to go forth at the wrong time.

kekaye.meaning_2: Kekaka; name of a country; name of a king
kekaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as kekaye, probably a locative singular or a sandhi variant of kekake. It is a proper name, the Kekaka country or its king, listed with Pañcāla and Kuru.
kekaye.example_1: 155. Tayo giriṃ antaraṃ kāmayāmi, pañcālā kuruyo kekake ca [kurayo kekaye ca (sī.)];
kekaye.translation_1: 155. I desire three forts and the territory between them: Pañcāla, Kuru, and Kekaka.

rathūmijātehi.meaning_2: whose chariot-waves have arisen; with chariots surging like waves; with a swell of chariot forces
rathūmijātehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi-style compound describing an army with chariots like rising waves; instrumental plural in the verse. The meaning is uncertain; PEU takes rathūmijāta as a compound of ratha + ūmi + jāta. Alternative reading sarābhivassabhi.
rathūmijātehi.example_2: 157. Gajaggameghehi hayaggamālibhi, rathūmijātehi sarābhivassebhi [sarābhivassabhi (syā. sī. aṭṭha.), sarābhivassibhi (?)];
rathūmijātehi.translation_2: With elephants like storm-clouds, with horses adorned with garlands,

abhidhāvathā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Second person plural imperative/indicative in the verse; the text's -thā is a metrical variant of -tha. Some editions read abhidhāvatha cūpadhāvatha.
abhidhāvathā.example_1: 158. [abhidhāvathā ca patathā ca, vividhavinaditā ca dantibhi; vattatajja tumulo ghoso, yathā vijjutā jaladharassa gajjatoti;(sī. pī. ka.)] Abhidhāvatha cūpadhāvatha ca [abhidhāvathā cuppatathā ca (syā.)], vividhā vināditā [vināditattha (ka.)] vadantibhi;
abhidhāvathā.translation_1: Rush against them, fall upon them, with various outcries and trumpeting elephants;
abhidhāvathā.example_2: Vattatajja tumulo ghoso yathā, vijjulatā jaladharassa gajjatoti [abhidhāvathā ca patathā ca, vividhavinaditā ca dantibhi; vattatajja tumulo ghoso, yathā vijjutā jaladharassa gajjatoti;(sī. pī. ka.)].
abhidhāvathā.translation_2: Let a mighty sound arise today, like lightning from a thundering cloud.

cuppatathā.meaning_2: and rushing up; and charging forth
cuppatathā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for cūpadhāvatha; appears to be a sandhi of cuppa (quickly/moving) + tathā (thus) or an indeclinable phrase in the Jātaka verse.
cuppatathā.example_1: 158. [abhidhāvathā ca patathā ca, vividhavinaditā ca dantibhi; vattatajja tumulo ghoso, yathā vijjutā jaladharassa gajjatoti;(sī. pī. ka.)] Abhidhāvatha cūpadhāvatha ca [abhidhāvathā cuppatathā ca (syā.)], vividhā vināditā [vināditattha (ka.)] vadantibhi;
cuppatathā.translation_1: Rush against them, fall upon them, with various outcries and trumpeting elephants;

vadantibhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written vadantibhi, an unusual instrumental plural ending -bhi after the present participle-like form vadant-; the bhi form is probably a metrical variant of vadantehi or vadantebhi, 'with those saying / crying out'. lemma_1 is the underlying verb; the form here is a present participle in the instrumental plural.
vadantibhi.example_2: 158. [abhidhāvathā ca patathā ca, vividhavinaditā ca dantibhi; vattatajja tumulo ghoso, yathā vijjutā jaladharassa gajjatoti;(sī. pī. ka.)] Abhidhāvatha cūpadhāvatha ca [abhidhāvathā cuppatathā ca (syā.)], vividhā vināditā [vināditattha (ka.)] vadantibhi;
vadantibhi.translation_2: Rush against them, fall upon them, with various outcries and trumpeting elephants;

viḷayhase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular present middle of viḷayhati, with vi- and ḷ for ḍ. The variant viḍayhase in the text is a scribal or dialectal form. The root √ḍah takes the sign ya; the form is irregular.
viḷayhase.example_1: 160. Mā bāliyaṃ vilapi [vippalapi (bahūsu)] na hissa tādisaṃ, viḍayhase [viḷayhase (sī. pī.)] na hi labhase nisedhakaṃ;
viḷayhase.translation_1: “Fool, babble not, for he is not such as that; you burn, for you do not find a restrainer;

papīḷitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used verbally in the verse; nominative plural agreeing with thalasā. The root is sometimes given as √pīḷa (Dhātvattha 235).
papīḷitā.example_2: Ghammābhitattā thalasā papīḷitā, tasseva pāde purisassa khādare.
papīḷitā.translation_2: Heated by the sun and chafed, they chafe the very feet of that same person.

tamhāka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of tumhāka. Genitive plural of the pronoun tvaṃ.
tamhāka.example_1: 162. Evameva yo dukkulīno anariyo, tammāka [tamhāka (sī.), tumhāka (syā. pī.)] vijjañca sutañca ādiya;
tamhāka.translation_1: Even so, an underbred, ignoble person, having sought learning and spiritual growth from a master,

khujjamakāmayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, referring to a hunchbacked woman. The form khujjaṃ is the feminine accusative singular of khujja. The reading khujjamakāmayiṃ is a sandhi of khujjaṃ + akāmayiṃ. Note: the root √khujj is not listed in the given root list; 'khujja' is traditionally derived from √khujj (to be crooked).
khujjamakāmayiṃ.translation_2: “Thinking him a bull among men, I desired the hunchback;

thuṇāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads viṇāti with variant thuṇāti (sī.). Likely a denominative or onomatopoeic verb meaning 'moans, groans' (as a lute with broken strings). 3rd singular present in the verse.
thuṇāti.example_1: Soyaṃ saṃkuṭito seti, chinnatanti yathā viṇāti [thuṇāti (sī.)].
thuṇāti.translation_1: Now he lies huddled, like a lute with broken strings.”

makari.meaning_2: O Makari; my lord; dear one (term of address)
makari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative address in the verse; the edition notes the variant makara (syā.) and makarā (ka. sī.), so this may be a sandhi or variant form rather than a separate lexeme. Treat as an indeclinable vocative.
makari.example_1: 167. Tvameva dānimakara [makari (syā.), makarā (ka. sī.)], yaṃ kāmo byagamā tayi;
makari.translation_1: “Now, my lord, you have caused this; the desire that I had for you has departed.

rerukaṃ.meaning_2: tusk (sawn by a saw); elephant tusk
rerukaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (Sī/Pī) of renukaṃ; accusative singular in the simile 'like a tusk cut by a saw'. The PEU entry suggests a connection with reṇu (dust) or kareṇu; unclear.
rerukaṃ.translation_1: This desire is now incapable of reunion, like a tusk sawn by a saw.”

nānīhamānassa.meaning_2: does not strive; does not exert oneself
nānīhamānassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + īhamānassa, genitive singular of the present participle īhamāna (from √īh, strive). Fits the verse gharā nānīhamānassa, 'there is no house for one who does not strive'. Sometimes analysed as na + nīhamānassa.
nānīhamānassa.translation_2: “There is no house for one who does not strive, there is no house for one who does not speak falsehood;

nābhaṇato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nābhaṇato is na + āha + nto (a word boundary between na and āha), meaning 'not saying'. The entry is for āha alone, the perfect 3rd singular of āhanati used in the sense of 'said'. The sandhi na + āha > nā should be noted. Some editions may read nābhaṇato as nābhaṇanto.
nābhaṇato.translation_2: “There is no house for one who does not strive, there is no house for one who does not speak falsehood;

anikrubbato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentarial reading anikrubbato of na + ikubbato, a genitive singular present participle negated by na; the text reads na ... anikubbato 'who does not harm'. A sandhi-by-negation rather than word fusion; the prefix is na.
anikrubbato.translation_1: There is no house for one who does not take up the rod, or who does not harm others;

upapāditaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally with khantiyā (instrumental): 'fulfilled by patience'. The PEU suggests a causative formation; the text is verse.
upapāditaṃ.translation_2: When that is joined with virtuous behavior (sīlena) and fulfilled with patience,

vikaṇṇakako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A name in a list of horses in the Jātaka verse (nominative singular). Possibly 'one without ears' (vi + kaṇṇa), though the commentarial explanation may differ.
vikaṇṇakako.translation_2: The Sandal, the Hunchback, the Ear-less one, the Black-eater (Asitābhū), the fifth is the Calf-hoof;

asitābhuya.meaning_2: Asitābhū; 'dark-splendour'; name of a princess (fifth of the five sisters)
asitābhuya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi/verse form of asitābhū (asita + bhū, 'having dark splendour'), a princess's name in the Jātaka verse listing of the five sisters; possibly a metrical variant ending -bhuya. Treated as an indeclinable name here.
asitābhuya.translation_2: The Sandal, the Hunchback, the Ear-less one, the Black-eater (Asitābhū), the fifth is the Calf-hoof;

bhūtapacaniṃ.meaning_2: cooker of beings; that which cooks sentient beings (craving)
bhūtapacaniṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (bhūtapacaniṃ). A difficult verse; the PEU takes the word as craving, which cooks beings. The final -iṃ might also be read as belonging to a different stem; the compound is treated as a whole, so the root fields are left empty.
bhūtapacaniṃ.example_2: Yo ca kālaghaso bhūto, sa bhūtapacaniṃ paci.
bhūtapacaniṃ.translation_2: But the one who has consumed time, they have cooked the cooker of beings.

āvaje.meaning_2: would enter; would go into; would resort (to)
āvaje.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in the verse (sace ... āvaje); the text glosses the phrase as 'if he were to enter'. Some editions read sacevajemampi = sace + āvaje + imaṃ + pi.
āvaje.example_1: So dūsako rosako cāpi jammo, sacevajemampi [sace + āvaje + imampi] dūseyyagāranti [dūsaye gharanti (sī. syā. pī.)].
āvaje.translation_1: He is a corrupter, a harasser, and a wretched creature; if he were to enter, he would defile this hut.”

rūhakaṃ.meaning_2: Rūhaka (the section of the Jātaka named after the Rūhaka birth story); sprouting one
rūhakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the verse, referring to the Rūhaka-vagga of the Jātaka; alternatively a name formed from rūha + ka ('sprouting').
rūhakaṃ.example_2: Daḷhañca vaggaṃ aparena santhavaṃ, kalyāṇavaggāsadiso ca rūhakaṃ;
rūhakaṃ.translation_2: The Daḷha chapter, then the one about friendship, the Kalyāṇa chapter, the similar one, and the sprouting one;

āvedhañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse āvedhañca = āvedhaṃ + ca, accusative singular. The commentary explains it as a wound (where blood flows); cf. āveṭhiya.
āvedhañca.translation_2: 3. I see no wound from which blood might flow;

anutāḷayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist in the text (anutāḷayi); causative of anutāḷeti, meaning 'to beat or strike with (an instrument)'. The PEU entry suggests a different analysis (anu + taḷa + ṇaya + ti), but the meaning 'beat' points to √taḷ.

tiṇaparighāsaṃ.meaning_2: grass remnants; leftover grass; grass fodder; remains of grass
tiṇaparighāsaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of tiṇa (grass) and parighāsa (remnant, leftover). Accusative singular in the verse.
tiṇaparighāsaṃ.translation_2: 10. Having eaten grass and the scum of gruel, having eaten rice-broth and rice-powder;

mahābramhe.meaning_2: great Brahma; great brahma god; Great Brahma
mahābramhe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative or locative singular in the verse (sandhi -e); could also be read as a plural. The PEU lists the senses 'noble brahmin' and 'noble merchant'.
mahābramhe.example_1: Bahuṃ [pahū (sī. pī.), pahuṃ (syā. ka.)] tattha mahābramhe, api ācāmakuṇḍakaṃ.
mahābramhe.translation_1: There, great Brahma, even rice-broth and rice-powder are much.

aposayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular, sandhi with 'ca' in the text (mātarañca aposayi). From poseti = √pus with -e; the spelling aposayi shows the aorist suffix -i (cf. esi aor).
aposayi.translation_2: for so long he lived a long life and supported his mother.

akhāṇisuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural, middle/active ending -isuṃ with negative prefix a-. The form is unusual; the text means 'they dug again and again'. Probably from khāṇati, a by-form of khaṇati (√khan, 'dig').
akhāṇisuṃ.example_2: 17. Te ca tena asantuṭṭhā, bhiyyo bhiyyo akhāṇisuṃ;
akhāṇisuṃ.translation_2: But those men, not content with that, dug still more and more;

tirīṭivaccho.meaning_2: Tirīṭivaccha; name of a rich man
tirīṭivaccho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; variant reading tirīṭavaccho. Nominative singular in the text.
tirīṭivaccho.example_1: Atha kena vaṇṇena tirīṭavaccho [tirīṭivaccho (syā. ka.)], tedaṇḍiko bhuñjati aggapiṇḍaṃ.
tirīṭivaccho.translation_1: But for what reason does Tiritavaccha, the one carrying a triple staff (tedaṇḍika), eat the finest almsfood?

tiriṭaṃ.meaning_2: Symplocos racemosa (a small tree producing dye); its bark; a garment made from its fibre
tiriṭaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in a Jātaka verse list; the -ṃ is probably nominative or accusative singular. Some texts read tiriṭakaṃ. The Indian tradition (PEU) connects tiriṭa with tiro + i + ta ('going through, covered'), but this is uncertain.
tiriṭaṃ.example_2: Janasandha kahāpaṇavassa puna, tiriṭaṃ puna dūtavarena dasāti.
tiriṭaṃ.translation_2: Janasandha, the shower of coins, and again the Tiriṭa, and again with the Messenger as the tenth.

kundalīti.meaning_2: name of a horse (Kundalī); (in some editions) name of a jack-donkey
kundalīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -ti is the quotation particle (iti), not part of the word. A proper name used in an example simile; variant reading gadrabhī in some editions.
kundalīti.example_1: Socati cirarattāya, vātaggamiva bhaddalīti [kundalīti (sī. pī.), gadrabhīti (syā.)].
kundalīti.translation_1: As Kundali mourned Windswift, she must mourn / For many a long day.”

aditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of dadāti (√dā 1?); here used in the sense of 'having seen' (√dis 1). The text has adisvāna as a variant. The form is aditvā (not aditvāna).
aditvā.example_1: Kathaṃ mūlaṃ adisvāna [kathaṃhi mūlaṃ aditvā (syā. pī.)], rukkhaṃ jaññā patiṭṭhitaṃ.
aditvā.translation_1: Without seeing the root, how could one know if a tree is established?

vinindāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd singular in the text (vinindāmi is 1st singular). Translates as 'I do not blame/criticise you', i.e. nāhaṃ tumhe vinindāmi.
vinindāmi.example_2: 54. Nāhaṃ tumhe vinindāmi, ye caññe vānarā vane;
vinindāmi.translation_2: I do not criticize you, nor the other monkeys in the forest;

vihiyyati.meaning_2: is lost; is abandoned; is destroyed
vihiyyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of vijahati (vi + √hā 1). Passive 3rd singular in -iyyati; note the doubling of y. Used in the stock phrase yogakkhemo vihiyyati; unmetrical in the verse, which may point to vihaññati (from √han, 'is destroyed'), a correction found in some editions.
vihiyyati.translation_2: Through association with a friend whereby one’s freedom from bondage (yogakkhemo) diminishes;

māhesu.meaning_2: let them not be; may they not be; should not be
māhesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Prohibitive mā with the optative 3rd plural of atthi/bhavati (mā + hesu). In the verse byagghā māhesu nibbanā means 'let the tigers not be homeless'. Some editions read mā hontu or mā hessu. Treated as an indeclinable particle in DPD style; pos could also be ind with meaning 'let them not be'.
māhesu.example_2: Mā vanaṃ chindi nibyagghaṃ, byagghā māhesu nibbanāti.
māhesu.translation_2: Do not let the forest be cut down, being bereft of tigers; let not the tigers be homeless.”

udditabhattova.meaning_2: like one whose food has been set out; as if with food prepared
udditabhattova.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of uddhitabhattova (= uddhita + bhatta + iva), the reading in the text being udditabhattova. A simile describing a brahmin with food ready.
udditabhattova.example_1: 67. Ko nu uddhitabhattova [udditabhattova (sī.), vaḍḍhitabhattova (syā.)], pūrahatthova brāhmaṇo;
udditabhattova.translation_1: “Who is this like one bringing food, like a brahmin with hands full?

sikhinī.meaning_2: crested; tufted; having a topknot (of a bird)
sikhinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it describes a balākā (heron); the text contrasts a crested heron with an ordinary one. Feminine form of sikhin.

punapāpajjasī.meaning_2: you will come to grief again; you will fall into misfortune again
punapāpajjasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of puna + āpajjasi (present 2nd singular of āpajjati, 'to undergo, incur, fall into'). In the text it stands at the start of a verse.
punapāpajjasī.translation_2: You will come to grief again, friend, for your moral conduct is just like that.

mabhisandhāya.meaning_2: what do you intend by this?; having what purpose in mind?
mabhisandhāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of maṃ (accusative of ahaṃ) with the absolutive abhisandhāya, in the sense 'intending; having in view'. The meaning given in the field follows the commentary gloss kimatthaṃ; the verse asks what aim he is pursuing.
mabhisandhāya.example_1: 82. Kimattha [kamattha (sī. pī.)] mabhisandhāya, lahucittassa dubbhino [dūbhino (sī. pī.)];
mabhisandhāya.translation_1: What purpose do you intend, in patiently enduring the impertinence of this fickle, treacherous monkey?

sujanādhiparomakadūsa.meaning_2: Sujana, Adhipa, Romaka and Dūsa (names of ten dice throws)
sujanādhiparomakadūsa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A string of four dice-throw names in the Jātaka verses, counted with satapatta and puṭakamma to make ten. Treat as a list rather than a true compound.
sujanādhiparomakadūsa.translation_2: Sujana, Adhipa, Romaka, Dūsa, again the Satapatta, and the Puṭakamma are the ten.

attapariccāgī.meaning_2: self-sacrificing; one who gives up oneself; who renounces oneself
attapariccāgī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of atta and pariccāgī, an -ī adjective. Used in verse as a nominative singular describing a hero. Sūro attapariccāgī means 'heroic and self-sacrificing'.
attapariccāgī.translation_2: As a hero sacrificing himself, I shall be one who obtains that.

duppasahajjime.meaning_2: hard for me to overcome; difficult to be overcome by me
duppasahajjime.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of duppasahajjame; locative singular agreeing with yatthaṭṭhitā (those standing where), meaning 'a place hard for me to overcome them'. duppa = du + pa, sahajjima related to √sah 1.
duppasahajjime.example_1: Te dāni saṅgamma vasanti ekato, yatthaṭṭhitā duppasahajjame [duppasahajjime (syā.)] mayā.
duppasahajjime.translation_1: But now they assemble and dwell together, and where they stand, they are hard for me to overcome.

lakkhivā.meaning_2: lucky; fortunate; blessed with good luck
lakkhivā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular of an adjective lakkhi(n) + vant (cf. PEU lakkhika), used for 'the lucky one' who enjoys the food; the -vā is the vant suffix.
lakkhivā.example_2: Sippavanto asippā ca, lakkhivā tāni bhuñjati.
lakkhivā.translation_2: The lucky one consumes it, whether skilled or unskilled.

vikattaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vikantaṃ is a variant reading for vikattaṃ, accusative singular agreeing with sūkaraṃ. The commentary glosses it as vikantiyamānaṃ chindiyamānaṃ.
vikattaṃ.example_1: 108. Vikantaṃ [vikattaṃ (sī.), vikantiyamānaṃ chindiyamānaṃti attho] sūkaraṃ disvā, sayantaṃ musaluttaraṃ;
vikattaṃ.translation_1: On seeing the pig being cut up, that flat-snouted one lying there;

udukkhalaṃbhikaṅkhati.meaning_2: a pestle and mortar; desires (a pestle and mortar)
udukkhalaṃbhikaṅkhati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of udukkhalaṃ (pestle and mortar) + bhikaṃ? Or more likely udukkhalaṃ + bhikaṅkhati? The text and commentary suggest udukkhalaṃ + bhi + kaṅkhati, with 'bhi' perhaps a prefix or emphatic. In the sentence it describes the craving of the maidservant Puṇṇikā. Doubtful analysis; possibly a compound of udukkhalaṃ + abhikaṅkhati. 3rd singular present.
udukkhalaṃbhikaṅkhati.translation_2: And that wretched maidservant Punna desires a pestle and mortar.

pottho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Jātaka verse contrasted with naggo; nominative singular.
pottho.example_2: Tadā naggo ca pottho ca, pacchā bālo vihaññati.
pottho.translation_2: Then, naked (naggo) and in rags, the fool (bālo) is tormented (vihaññati) later (pacchā).

makariṃ.meaning_2: name of a disease (in the nose); makara (sea-monster); crocodile
makariṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (nāsāyamakaraṃ). The passage is obscure; the variant reading nāsāya makaraṃ suggests 'a makara on the nose', probably a sore or growth. The PEU entry is uncertain.
makariṃ.example_1: Bhattu apacitiṃ kummi, nāsāyamakaraṃ [makariṃ (sī. nissaya)] vaṇanti.
makariṃ.translation_1: I have performed an act of reverence for my master, and I have caused a wound on the nose.

dhiratthumaṃ.meaning_2: shame on that!; a curse on that!
dhiratthumaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Cursing exclamation in the Jātaka verses: dhiratthu (shame on! a curse on!) + aṃ (that), sandhi of the final u with the pronominal element; the whole is an emphatic curse on the body. Written as one word in the text.

māsito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form is uncertain. The text (dumapakkāni māsito) needs a sense like "having eaten the tree fruits" in parallel with suhito; probably an irregular or dialectal past participle, or a sandhi/scribal form. Not the same as māsika (monthly).
māsito.translation_2: Just as I am satisfied today, having eaten the fruits of the tree.”

lohitapo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound with √pā (drink) as second member. Nominative singular in the text, referring to a mosquito or similar blood-sucking creature.
lohitapo.translation_2: Having arrived swiftly, the blood-drinker, lacking restraint, broke his vow.

anvito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used with 'parājayo ... anvito' in the verse, meaning defeat is attached to or follows the Assakas; the reading anvito is a variant for ajayo at that place.
anvito.example_1: 2. Jayo kaliṅgānamasayhasāhinaṃ, parājayo anayo [ajayo (syā.), anvito (ka.)] assakānaṃ;
anvito.translation_1: Victory for the Kalingas, who are hard to overcome; defeat follows the Assakas.

adejjo.meaning_2: not divided; not wavering; single-minded; unshakeable
adejjo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the verse; the text's abhejjo is glossed by the same sense. Nominative singular qualifying mano. The PEU entry is spelled adejjha.
adejjo.example_1: Damo samādhi manaso abhejjo [adejjo (sī. pī.), abhijjo (ka.)], abyaggatā nikkamanañca [nikkhamanañca (sī.)] kāle;
adejjo.translation_1: Self-taming, concentration, an unbreakable mind, and presence of mind when the time for action comes;

sampatthitā.meaning_2: was greatly desired (by); was much longed for (by)
sampatthitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably saṃ + patthita, past participle of pattheti used as a feminine noun phrase, meaning 'greatly desired'. The text form is nom sg fem. Related entry variant dabbasenā suggests dubbhisena may be a name (Dabbasena).
sampatthitā.example_2: 10. Pubbeva khantī ca tapo ca mayhaṃ, sampatthitā dubbhisena [dabbasenā (sī. pī.)] ahosi;
sampatthitā.translation_2: “Before, my forbearance and asceticism were sought by Dabbasena;

koli.meaning_2: Koli; name of a person (one of the ten brothers, sons of King Okkāka)
koli.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Jātaka verse. The PEU entry kola (palm tree; Blumea plant) is a homonym, not this name. The related entry also gives kolā (long pepper), fem.
koli.example_2: Atha koli palāsavarañca kara, carimaṃ sasamuddavarena dasāti.
koli.translation_2: Then Koli, Palāsavara, and Kara, and the final one with Sasamuddavara are the ten.

saṅkitabbāni.meaning_2: to be suspected; to be doubted; to be feared
saṅkitabbāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle used in the neuter plural (saṅkitabbāni) in the verse: 'saṅkeyya saṅkitabbāni'. The form is passive, 'things to be suspected'. The PEU entry is doubtful; √saṅk (doubt, suspect) fits the context.
saṅkitabbāni.translation_2: 44. One should suspect what is to be suspected; one should guard against the danger yet to come;

sampaṭihanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only in the variant reading sampaṭihanti (for sapati hanti) in this verse; a compound verb, so no single root analysis is certain.
sampaṭihanti.example_1: 45. Api kassapa mandiyā, yuvā sapati hanti [sampaṭihanti (ka.)] vā;
sampaṭihanti.translation_1: 45. Even if a foolish young man, Kassapa, should offend or strike,

manujesvapekkhiya.meaning_2: having observed among humans; having regarded in people
manujesvapekkhiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of manujesu (locative plural of manuja) and apekkhiya, the gerund of apekkhati. The text reads -svapekkhiya with elision; some editions separate manujesu apekkhiya.
manujesvapekkhiya.translation_2: Thus, observing that happiness and suffering in humans are unstable and unestablished;

ekabhattakinī.meaning_2: woman who eats only one meal a day; one-meal-a-day woman (variant reading)
ekabhattakinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (pī. = pīṭakasamuṭṭhāna?) for ekabhattinī; the lemma in the text is the reading with -kinī. Nominative singular, subject of abhikaṅkhati.
ekabhattakinī.example_1: Ekabhattikinī [ekabhattā kira (sī. syā.), ekabhattakinī (pī.)] sāmā, tameva abhikaṅkhati.
ekabhattakinī.translation_1: Sama, eating but one meal a day, longs only for you.

sīliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. Possibly related to sīla; PEU suggests 'virtuous person', but the context supports 'virtue/conduct'.
sīliyaṃ.translation_2: 84. Therefore, exert your effort, overcome your bad habits;

paṭirodanaṃ.meaning_2: crying back; weeping in response; counter-weeping
paṭirodanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The commentary glosses it as rejecting a request (yācanaṃ paccakkhāti), so the literal 'crying back' is used figuratively. Nom. sg. in the text.
paṭirodanaṃ.translation_2: The one who rejects a petition, they call that 'counter-weeping'.

paṭirodantaṃ.meaning_2: crying back; weeping in return; wailing in response
paṭirodantaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of paṭirodati; accusative singular in the text. The PEU entry analyses it as a bahubbīhi but the ending is participial.
paṭirodantaṃ.example_2: Tuvaṃ vā paṭirodantaṃ, tasmā icchāmahaṃ raho.
paṭirodantaṃ.translation_2: Or see you counter-weeping, therefore I wish for a hidden place.

ahāliddaṃ.meaning_2: not fickle; not unstable; steadfast; durable
ahāliddaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound with negative prefix na + hālidda; not a single dictionary headword. Text form ahāliddaṃ is masculine accusative singular agreeing with cittaṃ. The PEU gives 'not like turmeric-dyeing', i.e. not easily faded.
ahāliddaṃ.example_2: 103. Yassa cittaṃ ahāliddaṃ, saddhā ca avirāginī;
ahāliddaṃ.translation_2: 103. The one whose mind is not fickle, and whose faith is not transient;

kākātī.meaning_2: Kākātī; name of a woman (wife of Venateyya); name of a city
kākātī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name found in the Jātaka verses. The variant readings kākavatī and kākāti show textual uncertainty; in sentence 1 it names a place, in sentence 2 a woman. Nominative singular in the text.
kākātī.example_1: Dūre ito hi kākavatī [kākātī (sī.), kākāti (syā. pī.)], yattha me nirato mano.
kākātī.translation_1: Far from here is Kakavati, where my mind is delighted.”
kākātī.example_2: ‘‘ Diṭṭhā mayā, samma puṇṇamukha, kākavatī [kākātī (sī.), kākāti (pī.)] nāma devī samuddamajjhe vasantī bhariyā venateyyassa naṭakuverena pāpamakāsi.
kākātī.translation_2: “I have seen, friend Punnamukha, the case of Kakati, the wife of Venateyya, who dwelt in the midst of the sea and yet sinned with Natakuvera.”

kebukaṃ.meaning_2: Kebuka stream; name of a river (in Jātaka verse)
kebukaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a stream, paired with samudda in Jātaka verses 106-107. Accusative singular in the text. Spelling variant kepuka.
kebukaṃ.example_1: 106. Kathaṃ samuddamatarī, kathaṃ atari kepukaṃ [kebukaṃ (sī. pī.)];
kebukaṃ.translation_1: “How did you cross the ocean, how did you cross the Kebuka stream;
kebukaṃ.example_2: 107. Tayā samuddamatariṃ, tayā atari kepukaṃ [kebukaṃ (sī. pī.)];
kebukaṃ.translation_2: “Through you I crossed the ocean, through you I crossed the Kebuka stream;

samuddāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative plural samuddāni in the verse (satta samuddāni, "seven oceans"). The related entry samuddānita is a different word.

byāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in the phrase yāva byāti nimisati, meaning in the time it takes to open and close the eyes. The commentary glosses byāti as opening the eyes (byāti = akkhīni ummīleti). The PEU entry suggests the same meaning. The verb is rare and its root is uncertain; it may be connected to √byā (to open), but this is not in the given root list.
byāti.example_2: Yāva byāti nimisati, tatrāpi rasatī [saratī (sī. syā. pī.)] vayo.
byāti.translation_2: Even in the time it takes to open and close the eyes, vanishing (vayo) is occurring.

paaddhe.meaning_2: further half; further part; other side
paaddhe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (vatappaddhe = vata + pa-addhe). The commentary gives alternative readings panthe and bandhe.
paaddhe.example_1: 112. Tatthattani vatappaddhe [vata panthe (syā.), vata bandhe (ka.) vata + pa-addhe = vatappaddhe], vinābhāve asaṃsaye;
paaddhe.translation_1: There, in that vanishing state of the self, where separation is certain,

kāyasakepuka.meaning_2: name of a deity; name of a mythological being; Kāyasakepuka
kāyasakepuka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Jātaka verse it is a proper name listed among the ten deities, nominative singular. The compound is unclear; the second and third members are uncertain.
kāyasakepuka.example_2: Atha kāyasakepuka bhotīvaro, atha rādhasusīlavarena dasāti.
kāyasakepuka.translation_2: Then Kāyasakepuka, Bhotīvaro, then Rādha, and Sīlavarena are the ten.

tirīṭino.meaning_2: cicada; tree-cricket; ornament shaped like a cicada
tirīṭino.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading tirīṭino; the form in the text is genitive singular, but the entry is for the noun tirīṭī. The commentary explains it as from √tar with the suffix kiṭi. The title of the sutta is Kuraṅgamiga-jātaka.
tirīṭino.translation_2: When you, with sword belted on, in armour clad and wearing bark-cloth,

kuṭṭhūva.meaning_2: like a jackal; as a jackal
kuṭṭhūva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kuṭṭhu (jackal, nominative singular) + iva (like). The text's lemma is kuṭṭhūva; variant readings kotthūva and kutthuva are noted. The same verse uses gajamāsajja (having attacked an elephant).
kuṭṭhūva.example_1: Kotthūva [kuṭṭhūva (sī.), kutthuva (syā. pī)] gajamāsajja, seti bhūmyā anutthunaṃ.
kuṭṭhūva.translation_1: like a jackal, having attacked an elephant, sleeps on the ground groaning.

cīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ci (nominative singular of the pronominal/interrogative stem kiṃ, 'who?') and idha ('here'); used as a relative in the verses: yo cīdha = 'whoever here'. Sometimes analysed as cī + idha, but ci is the standard form.
cīdha.translation_2: Who here accepts the truth after examination,

saṃviditvā.meaning_2: having known well; having understood; having considered
saṃviditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of saṃvidati. Occurs in verse with attani ('within himself').

parikkhavā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in a verse; possibly a sandhi or alternative form of a word meaning 'discerning' (cf. parikkhaka). Not enough evidence to determine the exact analysis.
parikkhavā.example_2: Jappena mantena subhāsitena, parikkhavā so vipulaṃ jinātīti.
parikkhavā.translation_2: by chanting, by consultation, and by well-spoken words, being discerning, he wins abundance.

nevābhisajjāmi.meaning_2: is not angry; does not feel ill-will; is not annoyed
nevābhisajjāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + abhisajjati in the verse nevābhisajjāmi (na + eva + abhisajjāmi). The verb is 1st person singular present, so the entry is given under the phrase; see abhisajjati for the verb's own entry.
nevābhisajjāmi.example_2: 146. Nevābhisajjāmi na cāpi kuppe, na cāpi me appiyamāsi kiñci;
nevābhisajjāmi.translation_2: 146. I am not angry, nor do I feel ill-will, nor did I feel anything unpleasant;

nikaṇṇikā.meaning_2: whispering; speaking into the ear; private talk
nikaṇṇikā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it describes secret talk (mantanā) in the village, contrasted with counsel in the forest. PEU analyses it as ni + kaṇṇika, 'near the ear'.
nikaṇṇikā.example_2: 150. Yā mantanā araññasmiṃ, yā ca gāme nikaṇṇikā;
nikaṇṇikā.translation_2: 150. The counsel in the forest wilderness, and the whispering in the village;

cīti.meaning_2: scheming; plotting; this way and that; (reduplicated) iti cīti
cīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Echo-word of iti in the phrase iti cīti ca, expressing evasive scheming talk ('this way and that'). Treated as an indeclinable; possibly an onomatopoeic reduplication of iti.
cīti.example_2: Yañcetaṃ iti cīti ca, etampi viditaṃ mayā.
cīti.translation_2: And this scheming of yours—this too is known to me.

parisabbesi.meaning_2: crawls about; creeps around; slithers about
parisabbesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads parisabbesi with the variant reading parisappasi; parisappasi is 2nd singular present of parisappati. The form is a scribal variation of that form.
parisabbesi.translation_1: 152. You creep about like a one-eyed goat in a mustard field;

nuppajjatī.meaning_2: does not arise; does not appear; has not arisen
nuppajjatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + uppajjati; na + u → nu, giving the verse form nuppajjati (= na uppajjati). Present 3rd singular, negated. The buddho of the clause is nominative singular.
nuppajjatī.translation_2: 155. So long as the enlightened one, the Dhamma-king, the light-bringer, has not arisen,

alametehi.meaning_2: enough with these; these are sufficient
alametehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of alaṃ (enough) with the instrumental plural of eta (these). Here in the sense of being satisfied with or rejecting the mangoes etc.; verse 166 of the Jātaka.
alametehi.translation_2: Enough with these mangoes, rose apples, and jackfruits,

paṭikibbise.meaning_2: returning harm; wrong done in return; retaliatory cruelty; vengeful action
paṭikibbise.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse kibbise paṭikibbise, locative singular, parallel to kate paṭikate. paṭi = back in return; kibbisa = wrong, harm.
paṭikibbise.example_2: 170. Yo ve kate paṭikate, kibbise paṭikibbise;
paṭikibbise.translation_2: 170. Whoever, when wrong has been done, does wrong in return, and when harm has been done, does harm in return;

kuntini.meaning_2: female sarus crane; kuntinī bird; name of a bird
kuntini.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the text, addressed as a bird-name, possibly a proper name. Sandhi -i for -ī in the verse.

māgamā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Prohibitive mā with the aorist 2nd singular agamā (of gacchati). In the verse it addresses Kuntinī: 'do not go'. Sometimes written mā gamā.

māgamāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the prohibitive particle mā with the 2nd singular present of gam (gamāti = gacchati); part of the verse line vasa kuntini māgamāti.

maṇḍayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative in form and meaning. In the verse it refers to dyeing (nīliyaṃ maṇḍayati, 'dyes the hair dye'); 3rd singular present. Cf. PEU's Maḍi+ṇaya+ti and maṇḍeti.
maṇḍayati.translation_2: 173. The one who dyes his hair, tormented by the tweezers;

paṇṇuvīsaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka. sī. pī.) for pañcavīsaṃ, glossed 'twenty-five' in the commentary. A numeral in the accusative, varying vīsaṃ in the verse. Probably an indeclinable form.
paṇṇuvīsaṃ.example_1: 174. Vīsaṃ vā pañcavīsaṃ [paṇṇuvīsaṃ (ka. sī. pī.)] vā, ūnatiṃsaṃ va jātiyā;
paṇṇuvīsaṃ.translation_1: 174. Twenty or twenty-five, or nearly thirty by birth;

pacalaka.meaning_2: waddler; waverer; totterer; one who shakes or flutters
pacalaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A term of address or description meaning 'waddler' or 'waverer'. Vocative singular in the text. Used as a noun (or adjective) referring to a person, possibly with an implication of sluggishness or unsteadiness.
pacalaka.translation_2: How do you act, you waddler, so slow in your striving?

rājidha.meaning_2: O king; royal power; king's glory; royal majesty
rājidha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these Jātaka verses the reading is uncertain; possibly a sandhi of rāja + idha ('the king here', i.e. O king), or a corruption/variant of rājiddhi ('royal power'). Vocative sense in the address to the king. Compare rājiddhi in PEU.
rājidha.example_2: 186. Dūto ahaṃ rājidha rakkhasānaṃ, vadhāya tuyhaṃ pahitohamasmi;
rājidha.translation_2: 186. I am a messenger of the Rakkhasas, sent here to slay you;

yimaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of yamimaṃ, itself yaṃ + imaṃ. Relative-correlative sandhi; accusative singular of the bed (sayanaṃ) in the correlative pair.
yimaṃ.example_1: 195. Imaṃ so sayanaṃ seti, yamimaṃ [yayimaṃ (sī. pī.), yimaṃ (ka.)] passasi sārathi;
yimaṃ.translation_1: 195. That person sleeps in this bed, which you see, groom;

mabhipassasi.meaning_2: whom do you see; whom do you regard
mabhipassasi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of maṃ (accusative of amhaṃ, 'me') + abhipassasi (abhipassati, present 2nd singular, 'you see'); the variant reading is an accusative enclitic with the verb. Some editions analyse it as maṃ + abhipassasi; the entry follows the commentarial reading.
mabhipassasi.example_1: Sa ve rāja piyo hoti, kaṃ tena tvābhipassasi [mabhipassasi (sī.)].
mabhipassasi.translation_1: That person, O King, is pleasant; whom do you see as pleasant because of that?

kuṭidūsaṃ.meaning_2: hut-spoiler; one who ruins the hut; destroyer of the hut
kuṭidūsaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of kuṭidūsaka (one who destroys the monastery), used as an epithet of the cuckoo in the verse. Accusative singular in the text.
kuṭidūsaṃ.translation_1: Kāliṅga and Pucimanda, the hut-spoiler and the cuckoo;
